note: The breathy soloist and the one motif a track remembers (the research manual's section 4). A track draws one contour family by weight, one shape inside it and one phrase length (two or four fast bars, 2:3), each off a stream of its own; the shape's rhythm is written on the slow pulse (onsets and lengths in sixteenths of the fast bar, so an eighth at 87 is a quarter here). Degrees are scale steps from the destination, which sits on a tone of the chord in force; the first and the last note land on tones of that chord. A return keeps the rhythm and the contour (a recurrence), or the rhythm with a changed ending (a developed answer), or the contour slowed (a spacious statement), or the last notes alone (a fragment). Every number is a starting point for listening. The voice is a drawn row too: the breathy syllable by weight; the slow wavetable pad only where the bed already sounds it and the syllable would cost a second dear identity. What his showcase of 10-11 taught (a slow pad phrased like a human blowing air) is kept as principles: a breath-shaped attack, longer on a held destination; the mouth opening over the held note's own length; a breath between statements; a low-mid register; a gentle lid.
